summary: The marketing team is executing a China-first strategy, with the Intelligent China webpage launch and Asia Star program as top priorities, while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and managing a series of event and press deadlines this week.
summaryDetail: The most urgent item is the Intelligent China webpage launch and traffic drive, which is central to the team's decision to prioritize China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) over US programs for SEO and marketing. This week also requires closing out the Knowledge website redesign: Joseph must share the HTML concept, the team needs a 30-minute working session to mark feedback, and Joker will implement design changes, with the decision to keep the current design but improve menu categorization and article display. Event-related actions are pressing: confirm Prof. Tao Zhigang's Nov 13 APEC talk, review invitation letters, and send follow-up emails to TIA luncheon participants, while Julie must publish the LEED press release (after removing the 'first in Asia/China' claim) and opt out of the British Business Sentiment Survey. Looking ahead, the team must draft the SEO strategy brief, analyze participant and CRM data, and schedule calls with BritCham Shanghai and LinkedIn to explore partnerships, all while resolving the Outlook lockout to maintain email access.

Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic across the site.
Bring the BCI (and BSI) indices banner into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.

Display more articles on the homepage using a pinned/spotlight layout with additional latest articles below.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts; US programs (Stanford, Berkeley, Columbia) are secondary.
If a third priority is needed, add the Berkeley program for audit consideration.
